description: Who are you and what business did you start?We're Rachel Decker and Joss Poulton, cofounders of ClearSync. We help GTM teams take action on their Stripe revenue data in HubSpot. We're former HubSpotters who have been supporting, building, and using HubSpot since 2011, so we know...
sourceText:
We're Rachel Decker and Joss Poulton, cofounders of ClearSync . We help GTM teams take action on their Stripe revenue data in HubSpot. We're former HubSpotters who have been supporting, building, and using HubSpot since 2011, so we know HubSpot customers and their problems really well.
Our customers are B2B SaaS companies that bill in Stripe and run their go-to-market in HubSpot, usually PLG or a mix of self-serve and sales-assisted. Their founders, RevOps, finance, and CS teams want to know who upgraded, who downgraded, who's about to churn, and what MRR actually did last month, without exporting spreadsheets or hiring a data team. That's what ClearSync does for them.
Most Stripe and HubSpot integrations treat the systems they build on as ancillary and just copy over a snapshot of a few current fields onto the wrong HubSpot objects. We deeply understand the needs of our customers, how they want to use the data, and how Stripe and HubSpot's data models work. We rebuild a full MRR history, so every new subscription, upgrade, downgrade, and cancellation shows up in HubSpot next to the customer it belongs to. Marrying revenue data with customer data gets the right numbers to the right people, and they can report on it and build workflows from it. There are tons of edge cases and data integrity decisions you need to make when building something like this and we've accounted for them.
When Joss and I started talking about bootstrapping a company together, we researched a few ideas and kept coming back to one Joss had been living with for 15 years.
Joss has run RevOps at multiple PLG companies and kept hitting the same issues trying to see revenue data in the CRM. He kept seeing the product team pick Stripe for billing and GTM teams pick HubSpot, but nobody could get the subscription data into the CRM easily. There was no revenue context alongside the customer context that the GTM teams needed. We always say: "How can you do RevOps if there is no revenue source of truth in your CRM?" And there was no good solution on the market.
Since we're former HubSpotters who know the platform, its partners, and its customers, we decided to play where we have an unfair advantage. Joss is an archetype of our ideal customer and knows the pains and the market inside and out. My background is product and UX research, so I know how to turn a problem into a product. With all of this together, we knew this idea was a good fit for us.
We validated it the scrappy way: vibe coding a prototype and trying to sell it before it was really production-ready. We had a ton of great, actionable conversations getting feedback on our idea and building a prototype before it was ready for prime time.
Our launch was getting approved on the HubSpot App Marketplace in September 2025 and announcing it on LinkedIn. Joss and I shared it with our networks, and because a lot of our former HubSpot colleagues and RevOps friends knew exactly how annoying this problem is, the response was really warm.
We got some decent traction on our launch on the HubSpot marketplace, but the first dollar came from AI search. HubSpot's AEO tool recommended a content gap around a question people were asking LLMs about Stripe and HubSpot, so I wrote a piece to answer it properly. About three months later, someone asked ChatGPT about Stripe revenue data in HubSpot, ChatGPT pointed them to our blog, and they signed up. It was amazing. From then on, I decided to focus on AEO as a cornerstone of our strategy, and it has worked.
A marketplace listing gives you credibility and a place to send people, but it's not a distribution plan on its own. We expected more from it than it gave us, and I'd plan for that up front next time.
Content, on the other hand, compounds slowly and then all at once. Three months felt like a long time, but our content is still a cornerstone strategy. It also brings in better leads. People who find us through an LLM are already prequalified, because their search was so specific and personalized to their needs that they show up ready to use what was recommended to them.
Over the last year, about half of our customers came from organic search, LLMs, and YouTube. The rest came from our HubSpot network, partner referrals, the HubSpot Marketplace, and LinkedIn.
Our biggest channels are organic and AEO. We use HubSpot's AEO tools to see which buyer questions we're invisible for in AI answers, then write content that answers those questions directly.
Comparison content has been important. Our most-cited pages compare the different ways to connect Stripe and HubSpot, including the options that aren't us. We say plainly that HubSpot's free Stripe app is a great fit if you mostly sell one-time products. Buyers trust the truth, and so do LLMs.
YouTube content also works well for us. We made a video about HubSpot's free Stripe app because there was no information about it online, and we didn't even know much about it. We created that content, and it has genuinely helped people and generated leads for us. People find us through videos like that and they come away seeing us as a trusted source of expertise.
The people who buy ClearSync are RevOps and GTM folks who research carefully before they commit to anything that touches revenue data. They ask Google and ChatGPT detailed questions, so our job is to have the most honest, specific answer out there.
My advice for other founders is to track the source on every deal because you can't double down on what you can't see. Ask every new customer how they found you. AI referrals don't always show up in click data, but when we started asking, more people said an LLM pointed them to us than our analytics suggested.
First, we expected more good-fit distribution from the marketplaces than we got. We assumed being listed on the Stripe and HubSpot marketplaces would bring a steady stream of good-fit customers. It brought installs, but many of them weren't the PLG or hybrid SaaS companies ClearSync is built for. The listings give us credibility and are a consistent channel for discovery, but not conversion.
Building on an ecosystem also means you're always catching up. HubSpot and Stripe ship constantly, and every time they release something new on the revenue side, we have to figure out what it means for our customers and our product. You don't control the roadmap you're building on, so we treat each release as a reason to update our content and talk to customers about what changed.
We should have hired a real engineer earlier. I built a lot of the early product myself with AI coding tools. Vibe coding gets you about 80% of the way, but that last 20% is tough, and I held on too long because I wanted to figure it out myself. I should have spent more of my early time focused on marketing and sales.
Finally, cofounder fit is key. Joss has lived the customer's problem for 15 years, and I've spent my career figuring out how to turn problems into products. We are close friends who trust each other completely, which makes decision-making fast and easy.
The mistake I see most often is founders building a product before they deeply understand the problem underneath it. "Just sync Stripe to HubSpot" sounds simple and isn't, thanks to discounts, proration, upgrades mid-cycle, and every other real-world edge case. Find a problem that looks easy from the outside and is hard on the inside, especially one you or your cofounder have personally lived.

name: FeedHive
metaDesc: FeedHive is a social media marketing platform that helps users create and scale their social media presenc… — researched from public sources by Starter Story.
description: FeedHive is a social media marketing platform that helps users create and scale their social media presenc… — researched from public sources by Starter Story.
summary: AI驱动的社交媒体内容排期与发布工具，月营收2万美元。
insight: 核心洞察是社交媒体的内容发布需要大量重复性工作，FeedHive通过自动化排期、智能推荐最佳发布时间和AI辅助内容生成，大幅提升效率，满足个人创作者和中小企业的刚需。
businessModel: SaaS订阅制，按不同套餐（如Starter、Pro、Business）收费，月费从$19到$99不等。客户群体包括个人创作者、营销机构和中小企业，通过免费试用吸引用户，转化付费。
chinaOpportunity: 国内社交媒体平台众多（如微信、微博、抖音、小红书等），内容发布需求旺盛，但缺乏跨平台统一排期工具。可以本土化，支持国内平台API，集成AI文案生成和数据分析，定价更灵活，提供免费版加增值服务。
productArch: 用户注册 ➔ 连接社交账号 ➔ 内容上传或AI生成 ➔ 智能排期建议 ➔ 定时发布 ➔ 数据分析反馈
businessLoop: 【引流】：通过SEO博客、YouTube教程和免费工具引流 ➔ 【产品】：免费试用和低门槛入门版，用户体验AI排期和自动化发布 ➔ 【变现】：试用期后引导升级付费，通过邮件营销和功能限制促转化 ➔ 【留存】：持续更新功能，提供数据报告和客户支持，建立用户粘性。
getStartedPath: 第一步：市场调研，分析国内主流社交平台的内容发布痛点，验证需求。
第二步：最小化可行产品开发，先支持1-2个平台，实现基础排期和发布功能，手动测试。
第三步：上线后通过内容营销（如教程、案例）吸引用户，提供免费版，收集反馈迭代，逐步增加AI功能和更多平台支持。
